name: Stranglethorn Fever
objectiveText: Seek out Witch Doctor Unbagwa and have him summon Mokk the Savage. Bring the Heart of Mokk to Fin Fizracket . Heart of Mokk  ( 1 )

comments.body:
This quest can be started at level 40. You will find Fin Fizracket lying on the ground on the lowest level of Booty Bay. He is under an upturned, broken in half boat. He'll request the "Heart of Mokk", and will lead you to speak with Witch Doctor Unbagwa in Stranglethorn. 

If you haven't done the "Scaring Shaky" quest yet, get it from "Sea Wolf" McKinley in Booty Bay, because that quest requires you to collect "Mistvale Giblets" from the Elder Mistvale Gorillas in the area. You will also need to collect 10 Gorilla Fangs for *Each* attempt you make at the Stranglethorn Fever quest. SO, its a good idea to stock up and kill a lot of these gorillas for the giblets and gorilla fangs. 

To find these gorillas, head north from booty bay along the trail. Not far from the entrance, on the east side of the road, you should see some of the elder gorillas running around in a field. This is your home for the quest. Slaughter gorillas until you get the required number of Fangs (and giblets if you're doing that quest). 

If you have a group for this quest, you only need one person to have the 10 fangs and follow the quest. The only point for everyone in the group is to get the heart of Mokk, and the only way to spawn him is to go through this veritable "gauntlet". 

Witch Doctor Unbagwa can be found in a cave to the northeast of "Mistvale Valley", the place where you fight the elder gorillas. Once you click the "complete quest" button in the quest entry box, Unbagwa will begin spawning gorillas that will run up the hill at you. The first wave is 3 enraged gorillas (level 42), the second wave is 4 enraged gorillas and a named gorilla (level 43). The third, and final wave, is 5 enraged gorillas and Mokk himself (level 44). Kill Mokk the Savage, loot the heart, and you're done. Well, you'll have to kill his buddies too, but the important part is killing him and looting the heart. If you die after looting, you still win =o)

The reward for the quest is 5850 XP (at level 40-43), and a 30 armor, 4 stamina, 9 spirit cloak, called "Medicine Blanket".
replies:
Awesome post.

This quest is hard.  The wife and I managed to do it at lvl 40 (druid/rogue), though we ate a lot of deaths in the attempts.

It is purely an endurance run, and unless you have a lot of AE (i.e. a mage) in your group, be prepared for a serious fight.

We finally finished it when we saw a lvl 47 pali that had tried to solo it, fail.  So, we invited him to join us, and the 3 of us did it easily.

comments.body:
You only need to kill and loot Mokk to complete the quest, so make sure to focus your fire on him for the final wave since you can still complete the quest if you die after killing him.

Between waves you have a couple seconds in which you can eat and drink.  If you have a pet or ally, you can send him out to attack to give you a bit of extra time as all the gorillas will turn to attack them.
just so you know if you are 2 or more doing this quest.  You do NOT need 1 fang each. It is enough that one person in the group hand in 1 fang. Then the quest begins.
5850 XP at level 46, My Booty Bay reputation also "greatly increased".

This is pretty tough to solo, but I accidentally discovered something that makes it easier. After handling the first two waves, I was out of mana and nearly dead, so I ran away from the third wave with Mokk in it. Once I was out of combat, I drank and ate to full, then went back to start the event over and try again. Turns out, Mokk and his friends were still there beating on Unbagwa. They were all still hurt from my initial damage, and it was easy to AoE them down. It would have been even easier to single-target Mokk. Being able to leave combat and recuperate while the event is still going makes it much easier.

comments.body:
As a 46 rogue, I did have a couple issues staying alive for the second and third waves.  However, death is not the end of this quest.  During the second wave I was down to one gorilla before I was finished off.  As soon as I died, I ran back to the cave in ghost form and got back in time to see Unbagwa still fighting that same gorilla.  I resurrected and finished it off, and tried getting ready for the third wave.

Third wave comes in and I get killed off with four gorillas left, unable to kill Mokk before I died.  As the first death, I quickly ran my way back to the cave in ghost form.  This time, Unbagwa was killed by the gorillas, but they were still in that cave.  So I resurrected, quickly bandaged myself, and went right after Mokk.  I looted the heart and bolted from the cave.

So if you're having issues soloing this quest, just remember that if you die, it's not necessarily over.  Just make haste back to the cave and continue the fight if the gorillas have not despawned.
If Unbagwa dies, he'll respawn after a while, but you will need another 10 Gorilla Fangs to summon the waves again.

You need to visit Witch Doctor Unbagwa (https://www.wowhead.com/forever/npc=1449). He is in the cave just north of Booty Bay. You need to turn in 10 Gorilla Fangs to him and he will begin the summon. Waves of Enraged Silverback Gorillas appear and you need to protect him. The 1st wave is 3 gorillas, the second wave is 5 or 6. (I believe there are 4 waves, as of this posting, I have not yet completed it.)

If you're in a group, only one person needs to talk to the witch doctor.  After the waves of gorillas attack, everyone can loot the heart from the last wave of gorillas.

Buff up first, then let one person talk to the witchdoctor.  After the last wave is done, DON'T talk to the witch doctor.  Loot first, then return to Booty Bay.  If someone talkes to the witchdoctor before they loot, the waves of gorillas come again.

For those who need it, path up to the cave can be found at 34, 62

Lvl 45 Hunter is confused.

It seems that it does not matter who starts the quest, only who kills Mokk the Savage and is able to loot his heart.

I was taking a friend (mage) to the cave to start the quest (I had farmed the gorilla fangs before she came on) and an Undead warlock was already there talking to the witchdoctor (we're both human). 

I thought, "oh well, we'll just wait until this person is done". But then the first wave of gorillas washes over us. I cast Blessing of Protection on her and tell her to run and let this guy do the quest, but she just starts nuking as soon as the bubble is off. I was unhappy to say the least (thinking that we were basically doing the quest for someone else, a Horde no less) but hung in there to keep her alive (I'm a paladin). I have to heal her alot because she's pulling the whole group on her every time she casts. I get in my licks and consecrate alot to get the whole group, all the time thinking this is a waste of time because we were not the ones to start the quest. 

Well, we get to the end of the last wave and my friend is able to loot the heart off Mokk. I didn't know you could do that (if you were not the one to start the quest). I don't know if the Undead could loot it or not (his pet was in there fighting but I didn't see him cast a single spell). I specifically did not engage Mokk because I didn't want it to look like I was KS'ing his quest target (really I was just trying to not get killed or let my friend get killed).

So I guess it doesn't matter who starts the quest, even an opposing faction member or someone not in your group. 

Seems to me Blizz should make it so that only the person who starts the quest and their group should be able to loot the heart. Just seems fair.

Just solo'd with my 44 fury warrior, i found out some neat tricks that might help out.

on the first wave try to kill as many monkeys as you can before you get low on health once you do run away and deaggro all the monkeys that are left they will run back and start attacking the witch doctor bandage/eat&drink while he fights them for a while (he can take quite a bit) once you get your hp/mana back up go back and kill the rest of the monkeys

on the second wave stand back a bit and let him pick up the aggro on some right away kill what you can then run a bit then come back and kill the rest and bandage/eat&drink up before the final wave

on the last wave stand back and let him aggro as many as possible get the aggro on mokk and kill him fast loot his heart and run (or kill the rest if you can/want to)

I did this at lvl 43 (rogue) and I had a lvl 43 warlock with me

The cave itself is at 34,61.  If you don't have coordinates in-game, then that puts it south of Gurubashi Arena, east of the road, right in the northern section of mistvale.

Please take note, that when you get the 10 teeth and he starts casting, or whatever, you will deal with 3 waves of gorillas.  The first wave is easy-ish, with 3-4 40-41 mobs (no elites in any waves).  The second wave includes a mini-boss in the 5 gorillas, named Konda, and he (I think) is a 42 (not elite).  The third wave is very difficult - you get the non-elite boss Mokk the Savage, along with 5 friends - Mokk is 42-44, the friends are similar.

At this point, I'd say screw protecting the guy, kill Mokk, loot, and run.  You finish the quest just fine that way.

Ran it solo as a 47 Paladin.  Got 5850 XP.
where is exactly?
This quest should be an elite.
The cave is at 34, 61, as previously stated. Three waves of 40+ gorillas. Hard.

Here's a trick if you're a mage trying this.

First wave.  Stay behind the Witch Doctor.  When they start on him, get close and Flamestrike.
Cone of Cold, then back off to the wall.
If you have IAE or Blastwave hit that now.
Frost Nova to lock them in place and run past them toward the entrance.  Flamestrike again, and let them run at you.  Pick the nearest and poly him (the most important part) now back up again and you should be able to CoC again, by this time the first wave is dead or close to it, except for the one that was poly'd.  Kill the rest, leave your sheep alone.

Bandage if you need to, and re-sheep the last gorilla from wave one when it breaks.  Let your mana regen, DON'T use a pot or gem yet, just let it come back on it's own.  You're still in combat, so you can't drink.

After you feel you have enough mana back, fireball or icebolt the sheep and kill the last gorilla.

Rinse and repeat with the 2nd wave, you might need to burn a pot or gem.  If you do, take the time to wait out your cooldowns for the pot.

Repeat until Mokk appears, then nuke his a$$ to death, concentrating only on him.  FN and Blink away from the others, run until they give up, then run back and loot Mokk as they are pounding on the Witch Doctor.  You can help if you want, but it doesn't make a difference after you've looted the Heart.

It was a close one because I tend to draw aggro and do a good deal of threat. And no, I don't give a hoot if you disapprove of a gazeteer, because it might be helpful to rational players.

I did this because I had the requisite Gorilla fangs from Un-Goro Crater (the gotillas sit on about three mineral nodes, tending to run to Small Thorium). So I found the witch doctor easily enough (as you leave Booty Bay, stick to the road and look to the right before the Arena-- where the Elder Mistvale Gorillas congregate).

I buffed with scrolls and Crystal Spire, had an axe with Beastslaying that was sharpened, and had my Dog Trainer Gloves on (+20 Beast slaying). The first wave was a pushover: I did a Blood Rage going into it so I could Thunderclap. After the wave I had time to eat and almost healed up.

Second wave had a Konga, and knocked me down to about 25% Health. I had use a Superior Healing Potion so was unable to drink for the next fight. The wave with Mokk almost did me in. I sprang Retaliation and killed the big guy first, using everything from Rend to Mortal Strike (and keeping up the all-important Battle Shout, Demoralizing Shout, and Thunderclap on all of them). I did grab his heart, just in case I died. I was down to about 10 Health when the last gorilla was still swinging, so I hightailed it out of there. Good ol' Unbagwa finished him off.

The reward turned out to be slightly less good than the cape I was already wearing, so I vended it, but the Booty Bay reputation reward btought me to Honored. Can't beat that!
